It also grew the barrel with Sheet, Menu and SearchField, because three workers solved the same overlay/menu problem three different ways — when a family needs a control the barrel lacks, ADD THE PRIMITIVE; three hand-rolls is how one surface stops feeling built by one person. 32 real pages left. TWO RULES RE-PROVEN: a gate that inspects code reads the AST, never the text (ci:admin-ui rule D matched a max-w token inside a COMMENT, the same flaw as the gate written hours earlier); and a dead orchestrator is not a dead unit — the agents' edits survive on disk, only their self-reports are lost, and those were never evidence. THE RULE THIS UNIT PROVED THREE TIMES: when a subagent reports 'I could not reproduce behaviour X', that is a defect report about the BARREL, not an acceptable trade — it produced Combobox, keyboard nav on Menu, and forwardRef on Button/TextField. ADMIN_UI §6 says dark mode ships from day one and the P6 lock records 'DECIDED (Matt): ship both'. It is NOT reachable: nothing in the codebase sets data-theme (grepped app/, components/, lib/ — the attribute appears only in the two tokens.css files). Measured 2026-08-08 by forcing it pre-hydration: the admin's own tokens flip correctly (--a-text #1c2024 -> #edeef0, panes/charts/map all follow), but document.body stays lab(100 0 0) = WHITE, so every dark token would render light-on-white and the surface would be unusable. Two things to decide: whether the body background is the admin's to own (it comes from outside app/admin), and whether a theme control is wanted at all. ci:admin-contrast passes because it computes token PAIRS, not what the body actually paints — it cannot see this.

DATA ACCURACY. `listings` has NEVER been analyzed: pg_stat_user_tables.last_analyze AND last_autoanalyze are both NULL (checked 2026-08-08), so pg_class.reltuples is whatever the last index build left behind. Measured drift: reltuples 617,326 vs exact count 594,608 = 3.82% HIGH. This is published — getAllListingsCount() uses count:'estimated' because an exact count times out, and it feeds the admin 'Listings (total)' card and the listing-detail database summary. Both are now LABELLED as estimates and the DAL comment carries the measured drift, so nothing claims false exactness; but the actual repair is an ANALYZE on that table, which also gives the query planner honest statistics for every other query against a 594k-row table — worth checking whether any slow query is a bad plan from these stats. Not run mid-unit because it is a production maintenance operation that deserves its own decision. Check autovacuum settings on the table while there: never-autoanalyzed on a table this size is itself the finding.

OPERATIONS. sync_history holds 19 rows, ALL dated 2026-03-16, zero in the last 30 days — while sync_cursor.updated_at and max(listings.ModificationTimestamp) were both TODAY when checked 2026-08-08. recordSyncRun() has exactly one call site (app/actions/sync-full-cron.ts:387) and fires only when a FULL run COMPLETES with history done; /api/cron/sync-full is scheduled `0 2 * * 0` (weekly, Sun 02:00). So either no full run has completed in ~5 months, or it completes without recording. The delta sync (/api/cron/sync-delta, every 15 min, runDeltaSync) is what actually keeps listings fresh and never writes here at all. The admin panel heading was corrected to 'Completed full syncs (last 10)' so it no longer reads as all sync activity, but the underlying question is untouched: does the weekly full sync still finish? Check the cursor phase history and whether the run is timing out mid-cycle. Related: nothing anywhere logs delta-sync runs, so there is no operational record of the job that does the real work.
